entities.summary:
Pope Paul I was the bishop of Rome and ruler of the emerging Papal States from 29 May 757 to his death on 28 June 767. He first served as a Roman deacon and was frequently employed by his brother, Pope Stephen II, in negotiations with the Lombard kings.

Paul I played a pivotal role in shaping the early Middle Ages, particularly in the realm of European politics and the rise of the Papal States. His papacy was marked by significant events, including the recognition of the Carolingian Empire and the strengthening of the Catholic Church's influence in Italy.

Despite his relatively short tenure, Paul I's legacy had a lasting impact on the development of Western civilization. His leadership during a time of great turmoil and transformation helped to establish the Papal States as a major power in Europe, setting the stage for the Church's future influence in the continent.

Paul I's papacy was also notable for its cultural and intellectual achievements, including the promotion of art, architecture, and literature during his reign.

The papacy of Paul I came to an end with his death on 28 June 767, leaving behind a legacy that would continue to shape the course of European history for centuries to come.
